source_caption:
𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐁𝐨𝐲, 𝟐𝟎𝟏𝟖.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I’ve seen countless addiction dramas over the years, but very few felt as raw and painful as Felix Van Groeningen’s 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐁𝐨𝐲. Most movies about drugs are interested in the addiction itself. 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐁𝐨𝐲 isn’t. It’s about people. People standing helplessly beside the person who is struggling to hold on. That’s what makes this movie so special.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Based on the memoirs of David Sheff and his son Nic Sheff, this is a true story that proves addiction doesn’t care who you are. It doesn’t matter if you come from a broken home or a loving family. It doesn’t matter if you’re poor or privileged, smart or talented. Nic is everything society tells us should be “safe” from addiction. He’s intelligent, creative, funny, loved by everyone around him, and raised by parents who would literally do anything for him. Yet methamphetamine tears through his life like a hurricane, leaving everyone around him desperately trying to hold on to someone who keeps slipping away.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Steve Carell delivers what is, in my opinion, one of the finest performances of his career. Watching a father slowly realize that he cannot save his own son is almost unbearable. And Timothée Chalamet, who somehow manages to make Nic both incredibly frustrating and impossible not to love. He never plays him as “the addict.” He plays him as a son who desperately wants to stop hurting the people around him but simply can’t escape the drugs consuming him. It’s an astonishing performance that feels frighteningly real.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
What I love most about 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐁𝐨𝐲 is that Felix Van Groeningen shows addiction for what it truly is: confusing, repetitive, exhausting, heartbreaking, and brutally unfair. The overdoses, the lies, the shame, the relapses... they’re not presented as dramatic plot twists but as part of an endless cycle that nobody seems able to escape. And that’s perhaps the hardest lesson this movie teaches. Love alone isn’t enough.

source_details.title: Beautiful Boy
source_details.synopsis: Beautiful Boy is a 2018 American biographical drama film directed by Felix van Groeningen from a screenplay by Luke Davies and Van Groeningen and based on the 2008 memoirs Beautiful Boy: A Father's Journey Through His Son's Addiction by David Sheff and Tweak: Growing Up on Methamphetamines by Nic Sheff. It stars Steve Carell, Timothée Chalamet, Maura Tierney, and Amy Ryan. In the film, the father-son relationship between David Sheff (Carell) and Nic Sheff (Chalamet) becomes increasingly strained by the latter's drug addiction. Beautiful Boy is Van Groeningen's English-language feature debut. The film had its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 7, 2018, and
